final.memo:
We have reviewed this business and determined it sits firmly in our "too hard" pile. While the group possesses insurance operations, they are inextricably bundled with a portfolio of opaque financial guarantees that we cannot model or value with any degree of certainty [D01], [D06].

To own a business, we must be able to project its earnings and risks over a decade or more. Here, the company's own results show a $13.16 billion loss for the first half of the year, and its balance sheet is subject to collateral calls that are not bounded by its stated capital [D01]. Without the ability to quantify these potential liabilities, we cannot determine an intrinsic value [D01].

We do not engage in activities where the risk of permanent capital loss is unquantifiable, nor do we attempt to guess the outcome of liquidity crises [D01], [D08]. Our standard remains to buy businesses we understand, with predictable economics, and at this time, we prefer to hold cash rather than participate in this uncertainty [D01], [D08].
